title: Repora routing assessment example
summary: Point-in-time routing assessment demonstrating QART structure, risks, gaps, recommendations, tradeoffs, and traceable evidence without copying live GitHub state.

findings.title: How should AST selectors compose with route-first retrieval?
findings.description: The routing design needs source precision without allowing AST selectors to expand beyond explicit route and trust boundaries.
findings.recommendation: Treat path and trust eligibility as the outer boundary and AST selectors only as a monotonic refinement.
tradeoffs: Keeping route-first semantics favors auditability over fuzzy source discovery.

findings.title: Document routing has deterministic regression fixtures
findings.description: Route selection is represented by checked-in fixtures and validation code rather than opaque semantic retrieval.
findings.recommendation: Keep new routing behavior covered by exact fixture expectations.
tradeoffs: Deterministic fixtures require maintenance when route priority intentionally changes.

findings.title: Keep AST selectors as monotonic route refinements
findings.description: AST-aware selection should only narrow files already admitted by route include/exclude and trust eligibility.
findings.recommendation: Reject selector behavior that introduces files outside the configured route candidate set.
tradeoffs: This containment rule makes implementation context predictable but intentionally limits broad code discovery.

findings.title: Deterministic routing trades flexibility for auditability
findings.description: Exact routes, trust rules, and AST selectors are easier to reproduce and review than fuzzy or embedding-based retrieval, but they require explicit maintenance as repository structure evolves.
findings.recommendation: Prefer deterministic selectors for implementation context and add new selector families only when concrete use cases justify them.
tradeoffs: Explicit selectors reduce retrieval ambiguity while increasing fixture and routing-policy maintenance.

findings.title: Intentional route changes can drift from fixture expectations
findings.description: Adding or reprioritizing routes can change selected route order and candidate context; stale fixtures would either fail validation or, if bypassed, leave the change less auditable.
findings.recommendation: Update deterministic fixtures in the same change as any intentional routing-priority or selection change.
tradeoffs: Strict regression fixtures create maintenance work but make route-selection changes explicit in review.

findings.title: Assessment automation was deferred at this snapshot
findings.description: At the recorded repository revision, the assessment framework had not yet added report skeleton creation, report validation, finding listing, or scorecard projection commands.
findings.recommendation: Add assessment automation in bounded slices after the report contracts are reviewed and stable.
tradeoffs: Deferring automation kept the initial contract work low-risk but required assessment artifacts to be authored manually at this snapshot.

evidence.claim: Repora has checked-in deterministic route fixtures and a validator for route ordering and selection contracts.
evidence.rationale: The claim is directly supported by committed fixture and validator files.

dimensions.name: architecture
dimensions.rationale: The example is limited to the routing subsystem and uses direct repository evidence; it is not a whole-project architecture score.

dimensions.name: documentation
dimensions.rationale: Routing behavior is documented alongside the checked-in configuration and fixtures; this score is illustrative and scoped to routing.

metadata.notes: Example only. Findings describe the recorded snapshot rather than current GitHub state. Scores are explicitly scoped and must not be generalized beyond the cited evidence.
